newsitem.title: SPAIN: Telefonica signs digital TV group deal.
newsitem.headline: Telefonica signs digital TV group deal.

text.p: Spain's telecommunications group Telefonica said it had signed a final agreement with domestic and international partners to create the first digital television platform in Spain.

In a statement late Friday, Telefonica said participants in the deal were Television Espanola Tematica, Mexico's Televisa, regional stations Telemadrid, Canal 9, and Television de Galicia as well as other media groups Grupo Recoletos, Unidad Editorial, Cronicas P. Leonesas, COPE, Las Provincias and Epoca.
The preliminary agreement, which was signed in November, had included Antena 3 and Television de Catalunya.
"Television de Catalunya has reiterated in writing its firm decision to join the digital platorm once it has received authorization from the regional government," the statement said.
Antena 3, which was to have a 17 percent stake in the group, was not among signatories to the final agreement.
New members included Grupo Recoletos, Unidad Editorial, Cronicas P. Leonesas, COPE, Las Provincias and Epoca.
"Other companies and editorial groups have joined the platform to add in terms of numbers of business participants and of content," the statement said.

"The companies signing commit themselves to make the best effort so that in the future there will be one digital platform ruled by the principles of neutrality, equilibrium and non-discrimination," the statement said.
Telefonica said it would lead the technology part of the new group, while content would be managed by the television operators, who will guarantee competitive, high-quality programming.
Telefonica said it would begin to provide services of electronic press, telebanking, high-speed Internet connections, and tele-education during the second half of the year.
Once current tests are finished, the service will be offered commercially.
